likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) revamped **Integrated Ombudsman Scheme** came into effect on **July 1, 2026**, replacing the erstwhile 2021 framework to expedite customer grievance redressal and establish strict institutional liability.
Introduces a mandatory sequential escalation process: customers must first approach the concerned regulated entity (bank, NBFC, payment system participant).

If the entity fails to respond within **30 days** (or within specific timelines set by RBI/NPCI/card networks) or provides an unsatisfactory resolution, the customer can escalate the complaint to the RBI Ombudsman within **90 days**.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Effective Date:** **July 1, 2026** (supersedes the 2021 Integrated Ombudsman framework).
**Escalation Timeline:**
**Entity Resolution Window:** **30 calendar days** for the regulated entity to respond.
**Ombudsman Escalation Window:** Complaint must be filed with the RBI Ombudsman within **90 days** post the 30-day window or rejection.
**Statutory Compensation Ceilings:**
**Consequential Financial Loss:** Up to **₹30 lakh** (reimbursing actual financial loss arising directly from the act/omission).
**Harassment, Mental Anguish & Loss of Time:** Up to **₹3 lakh** (awarded to the complainant for mental distress, expenses, and harassment).

**Grievance Trend Benchmark:** In FY25, **Chandigarh** recorded the highest RBI Ombudsman complaint rate (over 4.5 times the national average), with **loans and advances** forming the single largest complaint category.
knowUnderstandContext: Prevents premature bypass of internal dispute resolution while enforcing significant financial deterrents against sluggish customer service. Replaces fragmented ombudsman schemes with single-window digital escalation under the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC).
examFocus: Exact compensation limits: ₹30 lakh (consequential loss) and ₹3 lakh (mental anguish/harassment).

### 1. RBI Revamps Integrated Ombudsman Scheme: Mandatory 30-Day Turnaround & ₹30 Lakh Compensation Cap

* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-07-01
* **Revision Effort:** ~10 min
* **Status:** IMPLEMENTED

#### What Happened
* The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) revamped **Integrated Ombudsman Scheme** came into effect on **July 1, 2026**, replacing the erstwhile 2021 framework to expedite customer grievance redressal and establish strict institutional liability.
* Introduces a mandatory sequential escalation process: customers must first approach the concerned regulated entity (bank, NBFC, payment system participant).
* If the entity fails to respond within **30 days** (or within specific timelines set by RBI/NPCI/card networks) or provides an unsatisfactory resolution, the customer can escalate the complaint to the RBI Ombudsman within **90 days**.

#### Must Memorize
* **Effective Date:** **July 1, 2026** (supersedes the 2021 Integrated Ombudsman framework).
* **Escalation Timeline:**
  * **Entity Resolution Window:** **30 calendar days** for the regulated entity to respond.
  * **Ombudsman Escalation Window:** Complaint must be filed with the RBI Ombudsman within **90 days** post the 30-day window or rejection.
* **Statutory Compensation Ceilings:**
  * **Consequential Financial Loss:** Up to **₹30 lakh** (reimbursing actual financial loss arising directly from the act/omission).
  * **Harassment, Mental Anguish & Loss of Time:** Up to **₹3 lakh** (awarded to the complainant for mental distress, expenses, and harassment).
* **Grievance Trend Benchmark:** In FY25, **Chandigarh** recorded the highest RBI Ombudsman complaint rate (over 4.5 times the national average), with **loans and advances** forming the single largest complaint category.

#### Know / Understand
* Prevents premature bypass of internal dispute resolution while enforcing significant financial deterrents against sluggish customer service. Replaces fragmented ombudsman schemes with single-window digital escalation under the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC).

**Contribution & Remittance Norms:**
**Remittance Deadline:** Employers must remit both employer and employee contributions (plus admin charges) within **15 days of the close of every month**.
**Contribution Rates:** Retained at **12%** standard (and **10%** for specifically notified establishments).
**Wage Ceiling Linkage:** Mandatory contributions remain explicitly linked to the statutory wage ceiling of **₹15,000 per month**.
**Streamlined Withdrawal Architecture:**
Withdrawal categories compressed from **13 complex heads into 3 streamlined categories**:
**Mandatory Minimum Balance:** **25%** of the total PF corpus must be preserved at all times during partial withdrawals.

**Illness Withdrawal:** Members can withdraw up to **100% of eligible balance** (which equals **75% of total accumulated funds** after retaining the 25% minimum balance) after completing **12 months of total membership**.

**Pension & EDLI Claims:** Mandated within **20 days**.
**Penal Interest on Official Delay:** **12% per annum** penal interest imposed on officials for delays exceeding 20 days.

Rolled out **CITES 2.01** (Centralised IT Enabled Services) migrating 340 million accounts across 120 decentralised databases into a single unified national architecture.
Auto-settlement limit for advance claims raised from **₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh** for KYC-compliant members.
Interest rate for EPF subscribers maintained at **8.25% for FY26** (credited by July 15, months ahead of schedule).

rbi-final-directions-non-recognition-of-.title: RBI Final Directions: Non-Recognition of Unrealised Interest on Specified Non-Financial Assets (SNFAs)
rbi-final-directions-non-recognition-of-.atomicRecall: RBI Final Directions: Non-Recognition of Unrealised Interest on Specified Non-Financial Assets (SNFAs)

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India issued the **Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Resolution of Stressed Assets) Third Amendment Directions, 2026**, directing all Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and NBFCs **not to recognise unrealised interest and charges as income** when acquiring Specified Non-Financial Assets (SNFAs) in debt resolution.
Prohibits artificial income inflation by preventing lenders from booking unpaid accrued interest into Profit & Loss accounts upon acquiring stressed collateral.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Definition of SNFA (Paragraph 6(15A)):** An immovable asset acquired by a bank in satisfaction or part satisfaction of its claims on a borrower, including Non-Banking Assets (NBAs) acquired under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
**Effective Date:** Comes into force from **October 1, 2026**.

**P&L Reversal Mandate:** Any unrealised income on SNFAs outstanding on bank books as of **September 30, 2026**, must be completely reversed through the Profit and Loss account by **September 30, 2027**, to the extent it remains unrealised.
**Disposal & Auction Rules (Paragraphs 13B & 140J–140M):**
**Mandatory Disposal Period:** Banks must dispose of acquired SNFAs within a maximum period not exceeding **7 years**.
**Public Auction Requirement:** Disposal must occur via public auction adhering strictly to the auction principles of the **SARFAESI Act, 2002**.

**Strict Related-Party Bar:** SNFAs **shall NOT be sold back to the borrower or its related parties** (as defined under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016), even if the asset ceases to be an SNFA.
**Own-Use Reclassification:** If an SNFA is put to the bank's own operational use, it ceases to be an SNFA and must be recorded under **'Fixed Assets'**.
knowUnderstandContext: Resolves an accounting loophole where banks booked non-cash profits upon repossessing stressed properties. Forces honest asset valuation, rapid collateral liquidations under SARFAESI within 7 years, and stops circular asset buybacks by defaulting promoters.
examFocus: Effective date: October 1, 2026; Reversal deadline: September 30, 2027.
Maximum disposal period for SNFAs: 7 years.
Prohibition of sale back to defaulting borrowers/related parties under IBC 2016 definition.
Legal framework: Section 35A of BR Act 1949 and SARFAESI Act 2002.

### 3. RBI Final Directions: Non-Recognition of Unrealised Interest on Specified Non-Financial Assets (SNFAs)

* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-07-08
* **Revision Effort:** ~10 min

#### What Happened
* The Reserve Bank of India issued the **Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Resolution of Stressed Assets) Third Amendment Directions, 2026**, directing all Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and NBFCs **not to recognise unrealised interest and charges as income** when acquiring Specified Non-Financial Assets (SNFAs) in debt resolution.
* Prohibits artificial income inflation by preventing lenders from booking unpaid accrued interest into Profit & Loss accounts upon acquiring stressed collateral.

#### Must Memorize
* **Definition of SNFA (Paragraph 6(15A)):** An immovable asset acquired by a bank in satisfaction or part satisfaction of its claims on a borrower, including Non-Banking Assets (NBAs) acquired under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
* **Effective Date:** Comes into force from **October 1, 2026**.
* **P&L Reversal Mandate:** Any unrealised income on SNFAs outstanding on bank books as of **September 30, 2026**, must be completely reversed through the Profit and Loss account by **September 30, 2027**, to the extent it remains unrealised.
* **Disposal & Auction Rules (Paragraphs 13B & 140J–140M):**
  * **Mandatory Disposal Period:** Banks must dispose of acquired SNFAs within a maximum period not exceeding **7 years**.
  * **Public Auction Requirement:** Disposal must occur via public auction adhering strictly to the auction principles of the **SARFAESI Act, 2002**.
  * **Strict Related-Party Bar:** SNFAs **shall NOT be sold back to the borrower or its related parties** (as defined under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016), even if the asset ceases to be an SNFA.
  * **Own-Use Reclassification:** If an SNFA is put to the bank's own operational use, it ceases to be an SNFA and must be recorded under **'Fixed Assets'**.

#### Know / Understand
* Resolves an accounting loophole where banks booked non-cash profits upon repossessing stressed properties. Forces honest asset valuation, rapid collateral liquidations under SARFAESI within 7 years, and stops circular asset buybacks by defaulting promoters.

#### Exam Focus
* Effective date: October 1, 2026; Reversal deadline: September 30, 2027.
* Maximum disposal period for SNFAs: 7 years.
* Prohibition of sale back to defaulting borrowers/related parties under IBC 2016 definition.
* Legal framework: Section 35A of BR Act 1949 and SARFAESI Act 2002.

rbi-master-circular-on-special-rupee-vos.title: RBI Master Circular on Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) & Cross-Border INR Trade
rbi-master-circular-on-special-rupee-vos.atomicRecall: RBI Master Circular on Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) & Cross-Border INR Trade

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India issued a consolidated Master Circular rationalising instructions across five previous circulars issued between July 2022 and October 2025 regarding **Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs)**.
Standardized cross-border trade invoicing, payment, and settlement in Indian Rupees (INR) under the Foreign Exchange Management (Deposit) Regulations, 2016.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Permitted Account Architecture:**
Authorised Dealer Category-I (AD-I) banks in India can open SRVAs for their overseas branches or correspondent banks resident outside India without prior RBI approval (subject to reporting).

**Dedicated Exporter/Importer Accounts:** AD banks maintaining SRVAs are permitted to open an **additional current account** for domestic exporters and importers exclusively for the settlement of rupee-denominated trade transactions.

**Transparency & Directory Mandate:** AD banks must periodically update details of all operational SRVAs in the centralized **SRVA Directory** published and maintained by the **Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI)**.

**Eligible Transactions:** Direct invoicing, payment, and settlement for all permissible current account and capital account transactions under FEMA. Surplus INR balances in SRVAs can be invested in Indian Government Securities (G-Secs, T-Bills).

**EbixCash Milestone:** EbixCash World Money became the **first Authorised Dealer Category-II (AD-II) entity** to receive a perpetual licence from RBI under revised FEMA rules, with trade remittances permitted up to **₹25 lakh per transaction**.
knowUnderstandContext: Eliminates exchange rate risk for Indian exporters/importers by establishing INR as a direct international invoicing currency, reducing dependency on US Dollar clearing channels and deepening foreign central bank investments in Indian sovereign debt.
examFocus: Permitted operational mechanism for SRVAs under FEMA (Deposit) Regulations 2016.
Entity maintaining the national SRVA directory: FEDAI.
First AD-II entity to receive perpetual RBI licence: EbixCash (₹25 lakh trade remittance limit).

#### Must Memorize
* **Permitted Account Architecture:**
  * Authorised Dealer Category-I (AD-I) banks in India can open SRVAs for their overseas branches or correspondent banks resident outside India without prior RBI approval (subject to reporting).
  * **Dedicated Exporter/Importer Accounts:** AD banks maintaining SRVAs are permitted to open an **additional current account** for domestic exporters and importers exclusively for the settlement of rupee-denominated trade transactions.

sebi-revamps-fpi-regulations-rupee-denom.title: SEBI Revamps FPI Regulations: Rupee-Denominated Fees & Intraday Mutual Fund Borrowing
sebi-revamps-fpi-regulations-rupee-denom.atomicRecall: SEBI Revamps FPI Regulations: Rupee-Denominated Fees & Intraday Mutual Fund Borrowing

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) notified landmark amendments to the **Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPI) Regulations** and **Mutual Fund Regulations**.
Replaced US Dollar-denominated fee structures with a Rupee-denominated regime for FPIs and Foreign Venture Capital Investors (FVCIs).
Permitted mutual funds to execute **intraday borrowing** to eliminate settlement timing mismatches.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Rupee-Denominated FPI Fee Restructuring (Regulation 43B):**
Substituted US $1,000 application fee with **₹90,000** in eligible forex equivalent.
**Category-I FPI & FVCI Registration Charge:** Revised from $2,500 to **₹2.3 lakh**.
**Custodian Fee Structure:** Shifted from an annual payment of ₹10 lakh to a monthly payment of **₹85,000 per month**.
**DDP Remittance Timeline:** Designated Depository Participants (DDPs) must remit collected fees to SEBI within **5 working days** of granting registration.
**Common Application Form (CAF) Update:** Mandatory inclusion of date of birth/incorporation to streamline automatic PAN allocation under CBDT rules.
**Mutual Funds Intraday Borrowing Framework:**
Mutual funds permitted to borrow funds intraday to bridge temporary differences arising from pay-in and pay-out settlement cycles across asset classes and forex transactions.

**In Addition to Existing Limit:** Operates over and above the existing borrowing limit of **up to 20% of net assets** of a scheme allowed for meeting unit-holder redemptions (which carries a maximum 6-month tenure).
**Additional SEBI Key Directives in July 2026:**

**Investor Protection Fund (IPF):** Depositories allowed to use up to **5% of annual income** from IPF for administrative and employee expenses; **at least 95%** must be ploughed back into the corpus.

**Mutual Fund-Only PMS:** Proposed new PMS category with minimum client investment reduced to **₹25 lakh** (vs ₹50 lakh standard) and applicant net worth reduced to **₹2 crore** (vs ₹5 crore); fixed management fee capped at **2.5% of AUM**.

**Security Transmission (QTP):** Quick Transmission Processing for claims up to **₹10,000 (physical)** and **₹30,000 (demat)**; simplified documentation threshold up to **₹10 lakh (physical)** and **₹30 lakh (demat)**; requests processed within **21 calendar days**.
knowUnderstandContext: Eliminates operational frictions in multi-market T+1 settlement cycles for mutual funds while de-dollarizing regulatory fees in Indian capital markets.
examFocus: Revised Cat-I FPI registration fee: ₹2.3 lakh (replacing $2,500); Application fee: ₹90,000 (replacing $1,000).
Custodian fee: ₹85,000/month.
MF intraday borrowing permission (over and above the 20% redemption borrowing limit).
Depository IPF expense cap: 5% maximum (95% ploughed back).
MF-only PMS thresholds: ₹25 lakh ticket size, ₹2 crore net worth, 2.5% fee cap.

61st-rbi-monetary-policy-committee-mpc-m.atomicRecall: 61st RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Meeting: Repo Rate Held at 5.25% & FPI G-Sec Limit Overhaul

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) held its 61st meeting from June 3 to 5, 2026, under the chairmanship of **Governor Sanjay Malhotra**.
Unanimously decided to keep the policy Repo Rate unchanged at **5.25%** with a **Neutral** monetary policy stance.

Concurrently announced landmark foreign exchange and debt market reforms: completely withdrew short-term, security-wise, and concentration limits on FPI investments in G-Secs under the General Route, and expanded the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).
mustMemorizeFacts: **Policy Rates & Ratios:**
**Policy Repo Rate:** **5.25%** (Unchanged).
**Standing Deposit Facility (SDF):** **5.00%** (25 bps below repo rate).
**Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) & Bank Rate:** **5.50%** (25 bps above repo rate).
**Monetary Policy Stance:** **Neutral**.
**Macroeconomic Growth & Inflation Projections (FY 2026-27):**
**Core Inflation (FY27):** Projected at **4.7%**.
**Major External Sector & G-Sec Policy Measures:**

**Withdrawal of FPI G-Sec Limits:** Abolished the short-term limit, security-wise limit, and concentration limit for FPI investments in Government Securities under the General Route. Merged 'general' and 'long-term' sub-categories into a single limit for Central and State Government Securities (SGSs).

**FAR Expansion:** Designated all new issuances in **15-year, 30-year, and 40-year** G-Secs and Sovereign Green Bonds (in 5, 7, 10, 15, 30, and 40-year tenors) as 'specified securities' under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

**PROI/NRI/OCI Equity Ceiling:** Increased the single overseas individual investor limit in listed equities without SEBI registration to **10% of paid-up capital** (from 5%), and raised the aggregate ceiling to **24%** (from 10%).
**Export Proceeds Realisation:** Restored the timeline for full realisation and repatriation of export proceeds to **nine months** from the date of export.
knowUnderstandContext: Stable headline inflation projections (5.1%) and robust domestic momentum (6.6% GDP) allowed the MPC to maintain interest rate stability. Simultaneously, removing legacy FPI restrictions deepens foreign capital flows into Indian sovereign debt ahead of global bond index inclusion milestones.
examFocus: Exact Policy Repo Rate (5.25%), SDF (5.00%), MSF/Bank Rate (5.50%).
FY27 Real GDP projection (6.6%) and CPI inflation projection (5.1%).
FPI equity ceilings under revised FEMA rules: 10% individual, 24% aggregate.
FAR tenors expanded: 15, 30, 40-year G-Secs and 5, 7, 10, 15, 30, 40-year Green Bonds.
Export proceeds realisation timeline: 9 months.

rbi-final-directions-commercial-bank-len.title: RBI Final Directions: Commercial Bank Lending to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) & InvITs
rbi-final-directions-commercial-bank-len.atomicRecall: RBI Final Directions: Commercial Bank Lending to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) & InvITs

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India issued the **Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Third Amendment Directions, 2026**, permitting domestic commercial banks and overseas branches of Indian banks to extend credit facilities to SEBI-registered Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).
Establishes strict prudential safeguards, exposure ceilings, cash flow covenants, and risk-weighted capital charges.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Effective Date:** Comes into effect from **October 1, 2026** (or earlier if adopted by a bank in entirety).
**Core Lending Conditions & Exposure Caps:**
**Overall Bank Exposure Cap:** Capped at a maximum of **49% of the asset value** of the borrowing REIT/InvIT (including underlying SPVs and holding companies).

**Operational Track Record & Cash Flow Rule:** At least **80% of the underlying assets** of the borrowing REIT/InvIT must generate positive cash flows from operations for a minimum of **one full year** prior to loan sanction.

**Repayment Structure Ban:** **Prohibited bullet and balloon repayment structures**; repayment schedules must be amortising and must not concentrate principal repayments towards the end of the loan tenure.
**Security & Collateral:** Loans must be fully secured via charges on underlying assets, assignment of cash flows, and escrow of receivables.
**Concentration Norms & Capital Base Sub-Limits:**
**Bank Aggregate Sub-Limit:** A bank's aggregate exposure to REITs is subject to a strict prudential ceiling of **10% of the bank's eligible capital base**.
**Risk Weights on REIT Exposures:**
**Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Treatment:** Domestic bank exposure to REITs is treated as CRE and attracts a risk weight of **100%**.
**Capital Market Exposure:** If the exposure qualifies as a capital market exposure under concentration risk norms, it attracts a risk weight of **125%**.

**Overseas Branch Lending:** Lending to REITs undertaken by overseas branches of Indian banks attracts a risk weight of **150%** (and is permitted only via syndication where the bank's total overseas contribution does not exceed **20% of the deal's total funding**).
knowUnderstandContext: Unlocks domestic banking liquidity for high-quality, yielding commercial real estate and infrastructure assets while avoiding speculative construction risk through the 80% operational cash-flow rule and the prohibition of high-risk balloon repayment structures.
examFocus: Exposure cap relative to asset value: 49%.
Operational cash-flow requirement: 80% of assets for at least 1 year.
Bank capital base ceiling: 10% of eligible capital base.
Risk weights: 100% (CRE), 125% (Capital Market), 150% (Overseas branches).
Prohibition of bullet/balloon repayment structures.
Effective date: October 1, 2026.

rbi-overhauls-forex-inflow-architecture-.title: RBI Overhauls Forex Inflow Architecture: US Dollar-Rupee Swap Facilities & CRR/SLR Exemptions
rbi-overhauls-forex-inflow-architecture-.atomicRecall: RBI Overhauls Forex Inflow Architecture: US Dollar-Rupee Swap Facilities & CRR/SLR Exemptions

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India rolled out a comprehensive foreign exchange liquidity package to incentivize overseas foreign currency mobilizations and shield domestic lenders from currency volatility.

Introduced dedicated **US Dollar-Rupee Forex Swap Facilities** for PSU External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs), bank Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs), and fresh Foreign Currency Non-Resident [FCNR(B)] deposits.
Concurrently exempted fresh 3–5 year FCNR(B) deposits from **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** and **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** requirements.
mustMemorizeFacts: **CRR & SLR Exemption on FCNR(B) Deposits:**

Fresh FCNR(B) deposits with a tenor of **3 to 5 years** mobilised between **June 8, 2026, and September 30, 2026** (including renewals) are **100% exempted from CRR and SLR maintenance** for the original deposit amount for their entire tenure on bank books.
Temporary removal of interest rate ceilings on fresh NRE ($\ge 3$ years) and FCNR(B) (3–5 years) deposits until **September 30, 2026**.
**US Dollar-Rupee Forex Swap Facility for ECBs & OFCBs:**
**Eligible Borrowers:** PSU ECBs and AD Category-I bank OFCBs with average maturity of **3 years and above** drawn up to **December 31, 2026** (window open till January 15, 2027).
**Fixed Swap Cost:** Fixed swap rate of **1.5% per annum compounded semi-annually**.

**Transaction Mechanics:** Multiples of **USD 1 million**; initial leg at FBIL Reference Rate on spot basis; maximum swap tenor coterminous with repayment up to **5 years**; no ISDA agreement required.
**Forex Swap Facility for FCNR(B) Deposits:**
Minimum tenor of **3 years and maximum of 5 years**; swap conducted at par at FBIL Reference Rate; **covers principal amount only (excludes interest)**.
Underlying deposits carry a mandatory **1-year lock-in period**; window open till October 16, 2026 (for deposits mobilised till Sept 30, 2026).
AD-I banks permitted to lend to non-residents against foreign currency deposits via offshore/GIFT City branches.
knowUnderstandContext: Eliminates hedging cost uncertainties for public sector enterprises and commercial banks while incentivizing high-value non-resident capital inflows to build resilient foreign exchange reserves without placing regulatory reserve drag (CRR/SLR) on banks.
examFocus: FCNR(B) CRR/SLR exemption tenor: 3 to 5 years (mobilised June 8 to Sept 30, 2026).
Swap cost for PSU ECBs/OFCBs: 1.5% per annum compounded semi-annually.
Minimum transaction unit: Multiples of USD 1 million.
Lock-in period on swapped FCNR(B) deposits: 1 year.
Coverage limitation: Swap covers principal only, excludes interest.

rbi-revised-framework-on-limiting-custom.title: RBI Revised Framework on Limiting Customer Liability in Digital Banking Transactions
rbi-revised-framework-on-limiting-custom.atomicRecall: RBI Revised Framework on Limiting Customer Liability in Digital Banking Transactions

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India issued updated Amendment Directions on the **Review of Framework of Limiting Customer Liability in Digital Transactions**, expanding protection beyond unauthorized transactions to cover all **Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)** across card-present and card-not-present channels.
Introduced a statutory compensation mechanism for small-value digital fraud victims and established strict timelines for banks to resolve fraud complaints.
$$\text{Compensation} = \min(85\% \times \text{Net Loss},\ ₹25,000)$$
mustMemorizeFacts: **Effective Date:** The revised customer protection framework comes into effect from **January 1, 2027**.
**Statutory Compensation Formula for Small-Value Frauds:**
For individual customers and sole proprietorships suffering net losses up to **₹50,000** in fraudulent digital transactions:
**Mandatory Reporting Window:** Customer must report the fraud to both the bank and the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal / Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 within 5 calendar days** of the incident.
**Mandatory Transaction Alerts & Shadow Reversal:**
**Mandatory Instant SMS Alerts:** Banks must send instant SMS alerts for all electronic banking transactions **above ₹500**.

**Credit Card Shadow Reversal:** In fraudulent credit-card transactions, banks must provide a **"shadow reversal"** (temporary credit) of the disputed amount within **5 working days** of receiving the complaint.
**Investigation Resolution Timelines:**
**Domestic Fraud Complaints:** Banks must complete investigations and communicate final outcomes within **45 calendar days**.
**Cross-Border Fraud Complaints:** Investigations must be concluded within **60 calendar days**.
knowUnderstandContext: Replaces the rigid zero-liability/limited-liability rules with an algorithmic risk-sharing mechanism that incentivizes early reporting (within 5 days) and ensures victims of phishing or social-engineering scams receive immediate relief up to ₹25,000.
examFocus: Compensation cap formula: 85% of net loss or ₹25,000 (for frauds up to ₹50,000).
Mandatory reporting deadline: 5 calendar days to bank & Helpline 1930.
Transaction alert threshold: Above ₹500.
Shadow reversal timeline: 5 days (credit cards).
Dispute resolution turnaround: 45 days (domestic), 60 days (cross-border).
Effective date: January 1, 2027.

* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min

#### What Happened
* The Reserve Bank of India issued updated Amendment Directions on the **Review of Framework of Limiting Customer Liability in Digital Transactions**, expanding protection beyond unauthorized transactions to cover all **Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)** across card-present and card-not-present channels.
* Introduced a statutory compensation mechanism for small-value digital fraud victims and established strict timelines for banks to resolve fraud complaints.

#### Must Memorize
* **Effective Date:** The revised customer protection framework comes into effect from **January 1, 2027**.
* **Statutory Compensation Formula for Small-Value Frauds:**
  * For individual customers and sole proprietorships suffering net losses up to **₹50,000** in fraudulent digital transactions:
    $$\text{Compensation} = \min(85\% \times \text{Net Loss},\ ₹25,000)$$
  * **Mandatory Reporting Window:** Customer must report the fraud to both the bank and the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal / Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 within 5 calendar days** of the incident.
* **Mandatory Transaction Alerts & Shadow Reversal:**
  * **Mandatory Instant SMS Alerts:** Banks must send instant SMS alerts for all electronic banking transactions **above ₹500**.
  * **Credit Card Shadow Reversal:** In fraudulent credit-card transactions, banks must provide a **"shadow reversal"** (temporary credit) of the disputed amount within **5 working days** of receiving the complaint.
* **Investigation Resolution Timelines:**
  * **Domestic Fraud Complaints:** Banks must complete investigations and communicate final outcomes within **45 calendar days**.
  * **Cross-Border Fraud Complaints:** Investigations must be concluded within **60 calendar days**.

#### Know / Understand
* Replaces the rigid zero-liability/limited-liability rules with an algorithmic risk-sharing mechanism that incentivizes early reporting (within 5 days) and ensures victims of phishing or social-engineering scams receive immediate relief up to ₹25,000.

#### Exam Focus
* Compensation cap formula: 85% of net loss or ₹25,000 (for frauds up to ₹50,000).
* Mandatory reporting deadline: 5 calendar days to bank & Helpline 1930.
* Transaction alert threshold: Above ₹500.
* Shadow reversal timeline: 5 days (credit cards).
* Dispute resolution turnaround: 45 days (domestic), 60 days (cross-border).
* Effective date: January 1, 2027.

rbi-financial-stability-report-june-2026.title: RBI Financial Stability Report (June 2026): Macro-Financial Health & Household Debt Dynamics
rbi-financial-stability-report-june-2026.atomicRecall: RBI Financial Stability Report (June 2026): Macro-Financial Health & Household Debt Dynamics

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India released the biannual **Financial Stability Report (FSR) June 2026**, assessing the resilience of the Indian financial system, systemic vulnerabilities, and emerging structural credit risks.
Flagged the exponential rise in **AI-driven cyberattacks** as a premier operational risk for banks and analysed the rapid expansion of non-housing retail loans.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Household Debt & Retail Credit Dynamics:**
**Household Debt to GDP:** India's household sector debt reached **45.5% of GDP** in March 2026, driven primarily by non-housing retail and unsecured consumption borrowings.
**Emerging Market Ranking:** India stands **4th** in household debt among major emerging market economies (behind Thailand at 87.3%, Malaysia at 69.9%, and China at 59.0%).
**Consumption vs Asset Creation:** Consumption-related loans accounted for **nearly 50%** of total household borrowings.
**Ticket-Size Distribution:** Loans with credit limits of **₹50 lakh and above** accounted for **44.7%** of outstanding retail credit.
**Gold Loan Surge:** Gold-backed loans emerged as the **single largest segment** within non-housing retail credit, driven by elevated gold prices and quick turnaround times.

**Capital Markets Prudential Measure:** Effective **July 1, 2026**, RBI mandated that bank guarantees issued to proprietary trading firms and brokers in capital markets must be **100% backed by collateral, with at least 50% in cash**, curtailing unchecked leverage in derivatives trading.

**NBFC Upper Layer Classification Benchmark:** Finalised **₹1 lakh crore asset size** as the explicit quantitative threshold for classifying NBFCs in the Upper Layer (UL) under Scale-Based Regulation. Withdrew concentration norm exemptions for Government-owned NBFCs (offset exposures attract a **20% risk weight** with State Government guarantees).
knowUnderstandContext: While banking balance sheets are well-capitalised, the rapid growth in consumption debt and derivative speculation prompted targeted macroprudential tightening (guarantee cash margins and NBFC Upper Layer concentration rules).
examFocus: India household debt-to-GDP ratio: 45.5% (4th in emerging markets).
Largest segment in non-housing retail loans: Gold loans.
Bank guarantee margin for stock brokers: 100% collateral with minimum 50% in cash (effective July 1, 2026).
Asset size cutoff for NBFC Upper Layer: ₹1 lakh crore.

irdai-master-framework-insurance-interme.title: IRDAI Master Framework: Insurance Intermediaries Governance & Investment Limits
irdai-master-framework-insurance-interme.atomicRecall: IRDAI Master Framework: Insurance Intermediaries Governance & Investment Limits

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) overhauled the regulatory and investment framework governing insurance intermediaries, establishing perpetual registrations with annual turnover-linked fees, strict training mandates, and expanded investment headroom for insurers in infrastructure and private equity.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Perpetual Registration & Annual Fee Formula:**

Certificate of registration, once issued to intermediaries (corporate agents, brokers, marketing firms, web aggregators, CPSC-SPVs), remains **perpetually valid** subject to payment of an annual non-refundable fee.
**Annual Fee Formula:** \(\text{Annual Fee} = \max(₹10,000,\ 0.04\% \times \text{Commission \& receipts from insurers in preceding FY})\)
**Training Mandate for Insurance Marketing Firms (IMFs):**
Principal officers and insurance salespersons must complete at least **25 hours of training once every three years** through an IRDAI-recognised examination body.
**Insurer Investment Limits & Exposure Ceilings:**
**Infrastructure SPVs:** Insurers permitted to invest up to **20%** in operational infrastructure special purpose vehicles (SPVs) rated **AA or above**.

**Private Companies, AIFs & VCFs:** Combined investment limit in private limited companies, Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), and Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) is capped at **3% of investment assets for life insurers** and **5% for general insurers**.
**Promoter Group Exposure:** Overall exposure to promoter groups is capped at **5% of total investment assets**.
**Repo & G-Sec Lending:** Repo and government securities lending transactions are capped at **25% of available securities or ₹10,000 crore**, whichever is lower.
knowUnderstandContext: Shifts the regulatory model from repetitive periodic license renewals to continuous compliance backed by an annual turnover-linked fee and mandatory ongoing professional training (25 hrs/3 yrs).
examFocus: Intermediary annual fee formula: higher of ₹10,000 or 0.04% of receipts.
Training requirement for marketing firms: 25 hours every 3 years.
Insurer investment limits in Private Cos/AIFs/VCFs: 3% (Life) vs 5% (General).
Infrastructure SPV cap: 20% (for AA-rated or above).
Promoter group ceiling: 5% of investment assets.

* The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) overhauled the regulatory and investment framework governing insurance intermediaries, establishing perpetual registrations with annual turnover-linked fees, strict training mandates, and expanded investment headroom for insurers in infrastructure and private equity.

#### Must Memorize
* **Perpetual Registration & Annual Fee Formula:**
  * Certificate of registration, once issued to intermediaries (corporate agents, brokers, marketing firms, web aggregators, CPSC-SPVs), remains **perpetually valid** subject to payment of an annual non-refundable fee.
  * **Annual Fee Formula:** \(\text{Annual Fee} = \max(₹10,000,\ 0.04\% \times \text{Commission \& receipts from insurers in preceding FY})\)
* **Training Mandate for Insurance Marketing Firms (IMFs):**
  * Principal officers and insurance salespersons must complete at least **25 hours of training once every three years** through an IRDAI-recognised examination body.
* **Insurer Investment Limits & Exposure Ceilings:**
  * **Infrastructure SPVs:** Insurers permitted to invest up to **20%** in operational infrastructure special purpose vehicles (SPVs) rated **AA or above**.
  * **Private Companies, AIFs & VCFs:** Combined investment limit in private limited companies, Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), and Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) is capped at **3% of investment assets for life insurers** and **5% for general insurers**.
  * **Promoter Group Exposure:** Overall exposure to promoter groups is capped at **5% of total investment assets**.
  * **Repo & G-Sec Lending:** Repo and government securities lending transactions are capped at **25% of available securities or ₹10,000 crore**, whichever is lower.

#### Know / Understand
* Shifts the regulatory model from repetitive periodic license renewals to continuous compliance backed by an annual turnover-linked fee and mandatory ongoing professional training (25 hrs/3 yrs).

digital-personal-data-protection-dpdp-ac.atomicRecall: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023: Statutory Penalties & Regulatory Framework

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: Comprehensive enforcement guidelines under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA), establishing statutory compliance standards and high-quantum monetary penalties for data fiduciaries across banking, fintech, and commercial sectors.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Statutory Penalty Thresholds:**
**Security Failure (Data Breach):** Failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches attracts a maximum penalty of up to **₹250 crore**.
**Breach Notification Failure:** Failure to notify the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) and affected individuals in the event of a breach attracts a penalty of up to **₹200 crore**.
**Non-Fulfillment of Children's Data Duties:** Maximum penalty of up to **₹200 crore**.
**General Non-Compliance:** Penalty of up to **₹50 crore** for other residual violations.
**Scope & Applicability:**
Applies to all digital personal data processed within India, including employee data, customer KYC data, and digital transaction trails across both private and public entities.
knowUnderstandContext: Imposes massive balance-sheet accountability on banks and fintechs handling customer financial and identity data, making cybersecurity safeguards a top board-level governance requirement.
examFocus: Maximum penalty for failure to prevent personal data breach: ₹250 crore.
Maximum penalty for failure to notify data breach: ₹200 crore.

pfrda-digital-architecture-nps-pride-dis.atomicRecall: PFRDA Digital Architecture: NPS PRIDE-Disha & Pension Sahayak Redressal

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) rolled out two major digital platforms—**NPS PRIDE-Disha** and **Pension Sahayak**—to modernize fund performance benchmarking and institutionalize a structured, multi-tier grievance escalation mechanism for National Pension System (NPS), Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) subscribers.
mustMemorizeFacts: **NPS PRIDE-Disha (Performance Decision Support):**

Uses the **Extended Internal Rate of Return (XIRR)** methodology to benchmark historical pension fund performance against actual periodic subscriber contribution cashflows (replacing point-to-point CAGR which misrepresents regular monthly deposits).
**Pension Sahayak (AI Grievance Management System):**
Replaces the legacy grievance platform.
**Strict Two-Tier Escalation Timeline:**
**Tier 1 (Intermediary):** Point of Presence (PoP) or Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA) must resolve the subscriber complaint within **30 days**.
**Tier 2 (NPS Trust Escalation):** If unresolved or dissatisfied after 30 days, escalated to NPS Trust, which must issue a formal response within **21 days**.
Integrated with the Government's **Bhashini platform** to offer multi-lingual text and voice assistance across **22 Indian languages**.
knowUnderstandContext: Moves pension evaluation from static point-to-point percentage gains to actual investor cashflow returns (XIRR), and enforces binding SLAs on pension intermediaries through AI-driven escalation.
examFocus: PRIDE-Disha methodology: Extended Internal Rate of Return (XIRR).
Pension Sahayak resolution timelines: 30 days for Intermediaries $\to$ 21 days for NPS Trust.

pfrda-digital-architecture-nps-pride-dis.contentMarkdown:
### 1. PFRDA Digital Architecture: NPS PRIDE-Disha & Pension Sahayak Redressal
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** PENSION_SYSTEMS
* **Institution:** PFRDA
* **Event Date:** 2026-07-12
* **Revision Effort:** ~7 min
* **Status:** IMPLEMENTED

#### What Happened
* The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) rolled out two major digital platforms—**NPS PRIDE-Disha** and **Pension Sahayak**—to modernize fund performance benchmarking and institutionalize a structured, multi-tier grievance escalation mechanism for National Pension System (NPS), Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) subscribers.

#### Must Memorize
* **NPS PRIDE-Disha (Performance Decision Support):**
  * Uses the **Extended Internal Rate of Return (XIRR)** methodology to benchmark historical pension fund performance against actual periodic subscriber contribution cashflows (replacing point-to-point CAGR which misrepresents regular monthly deposits).
* **Pension Sahayak (AI Grievance Management System):**
  * Replaces the legacy grievance platform.
  * **Strict Two-Tier Escalation Timeline:**
    * **Tier 1 (Intermediary):** Point of Presence (PoP) or Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA) must resolve the subscriber complaint within **30 days**.
    * **Tier 2 (NPS Trust Escalation):** If unresolved or dissatisfied after 30 days, escalated to NPS Trust, which must issue a formal response within **21 days**.
  * Integrated with the Government's **Bhashini platform** to offer multi-lingual text and voice assistance across **22 Indian languages**.

#### Know / Understand
* Moves pension evaluation from static point-to-point percentage gains to actual investor cashflow returns (XIRR), and enforces binding SLAs on pension intermediaries through AI-driven escalation.

#### Exam Focus
* PRIDE-Disha methodology: Extended Internal Rate of Return (XIRR).
* Pension Sahayak resolution timelines: 30 days for Intermediaries $\to$ 21 days for NPS Trust.
* Language coverage: 22 languages via Bhashini.

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: SEBI notified structural investor-protection norms streamlining the transmission of securities for deceased investor legal heirs through **Quick Transmission Processing (QTP)**, while closing market-manipulation loopholes by enforcing an automated **ISIN-level freeze on promoter shareholdings** during share buybacks.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Quick Transmission Processing (QTP) Thresholds:**
Fast-track transmission under simplified documentation applies to claims involving:
**Physical Securities:** Value up to **₹10,000**.
**Demat Holdings:** Value up to **₹30,000**.
**ISIN-Level Promoter Buyback Freeze:**

Promoter and promoter group holdings (including associates) are **frozen at the ISIN level in depositories** from the date the Board of Directors or shareholders approve the buyback until the offer officially closes.
Prevents insider trading and front-running during the sensitive buyback execution window.
**SCORES 2.0 Redressal SLA:**
Regulated entities and listed companies must submit a binding **Action Taken Report (ATR) within 21 days** of receiving an investor grievance on SCORES.
examFocus: QTP monetary limits: ₹10,000 (Physical) vs ₹30,000 (Demat).
Promoter buyback freeze: Applies from Board/Shareholder approval date until offer closure.
SCORES 2.0 ATR timeline: 21 days.

sebi-revised-commodity-etf-framework-dyn.title: SEBI Revised Commodity ETF Framework: Dynamic Price Bands & Pre-Open Auction
sebi-revised-commodity-etf-framework-dyn.atomicRecall: SEBI Revised Commodity ETF Framework: Dynamic Price Bands & Pre-Open Auction

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: SEBI overhauled the trading framework for commodity Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), introducing dynamic price bands, objective base-price calculation methodologies, and a pre-open call auction mechanism to eliminate pricing anomalies and align secondary ETF market trading with underlying physical and commodity futures prices.
1. Base price is determined as the **Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP)** of trades executed during the **last 30 minutes of trading** on the previous trading day.
2. If no trades occur in the last 30 minutes $\longrightarrow$ **Last Traded Price (LTP)** of the previous trading day is used.
3. If no trades occur throughout the entire trading day $\longrightarrow$ Latest available **closing Net Asset Value (NAV)** serves as base price.
4. Exchanges and AMCs must transition to using **$T-1$ day closing NAV** as the universal base price from **April 1, 2027**.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Dynamic Price Bands Architecture:**
For equity and debt ETFs (excluding overnight and liquid ETFs), SEBI instituted **dynamic price bands with an initial limit of $\pm 10\%$**.
The price band can be expanded up to **$\pm 20\%$** following a mandatory cooling-off period:
**15-minute cooling-off period** if the ETF price moves $9.90\%$ or more from the base price during normal trading.
**5-minute cooling-off period** if such extreme movement occurs during the **final 30 minutes** of trading.
Overnight and liquid ETFs continue to operate under a **fixed price band of $\pm 5\%$**.
**Base Price Calculation Hierarchy:**
**Effective Date:** **September 1, 2026**.
knowUnderstandContext: Protects retail investors from execution slippage in illiquid commodity ETFs by capping intraday swings with cooling-off triggers and anchoring prices to 30-minute VWAP.
examFocus: Initial dynamic price band for ETFs: $\pm 10\%$ (expandable to $\pm 20\%$).
Fixed price band for overnight/liquid ETFs: $\pm 5\%$.

sebi-revised-commodity-etf-framework-dyn.contentMarkdown:
### 1. SEBI Revised Commodity ETF Framework: Dynamic Price Bands & Pre-Open Auction
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** CAPITAL_MARKETS
* **Institution:** SEBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-06-18
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* SEBI overhauled the trading framework for commodity Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), introducing dynamic price bands, objective base-price calculation methodologies, and a pre-open call auction mechanism to eliminate pricing anomalies and align secondary ETF market trading with underlying physical and commodity futures prices.

#### Must Memorize
* **Dynamic Price Bands Architecture:**
  * For equity and debt ETFs (excluding overnight and liquid ETFs), SEBI instituted **dynamic price bands with an initial limit of $\pm 10\%$**.
  * The price band can be expanded up to **$\pm 20\%$** following a mandatory cooling-off period:
    * **15-minute cooling-off period** if the ETF price moves $9.90\%$ or more from the base price during normal trading.
    * **5-minute cooling-off period** if such extreme movement occurs during the **final 30 minutes** of trading.
  * Overnight and liquid ETFs continue to operate under a **fixed price band of $\pm 5\%$**.
* **Base Price Calculation Hierarchy:**
  1. Base price is determined as the **Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP)** of trades executed during the **last 30 minutes of trading** on the previous trading day.
  2. If no trades occur in the last 30 minutes $\longrightarrow$ **Last Traded Price (LTP)** of the previous trading day is used.
  3. If no trades occur throughout the entire trading day $\longrightarrow$ Latest available **closing Net Asset Value (NAV)** serves as base price.
  4. Exchanges and AMCs must transition to using **$T-1$ day closing NAV** as the universal base price from **April 1, 2027**.
* **Effective Date:** **September 1, 2026**.

#### Know / Understand
* Protects retail investors from execution slippage in illiquid commodity ETFs by capping intraday swings with cooling-off triggers and anchoring prices to 30-minute VWAP.

#### Exam Focus
* Initial dynamic price band for ETFs: $\pm 10\%$ (expandable to $\pm 20\%$).
* Fixed price band for overnight/liquid ETFs: $\pm 5\%$.
* Cooling-off duration: 15 minutes (normal) vs 5 minutes (last 30 mins).
* Base price fallback: 30-min VWAP $\to$ LTP $\to$ Closing NAV $\to$ T-1 NAV (by April 2027).

rbi-master-directions-payment-system-ope.title: RBI Master Directions: Payment System Operators (PSO) Perpetual Licensing & Governance
rbi-master-directions-payment-system-ope.atomicRecall: RBI Master Directions: Payment System Operators (PSO) Perpetual Licensing & Governance

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued comprehensive Master Directions on Authorisation to Operate a Payment System, granting perpetual operational validity to compliant Payment System Operators (PSOs) while imposing strict cross-border investment caps on FATF non-compliant jurisdictions.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Perpetual Licensing Norms:**
Authorisations granted to new PSOs will be **perpetually valid** (removing periodic renewal bureaucracy).
Existing operators receive perpetual validity upon renewal provided they meet regulatory criteria with no supervisory concerns; non-compliant operators receive only **1-year temporary renewals**.
**FATF Non-Compliant Jurisdiction Safeguards:**
Investors originating from jurisdictions identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) as non-compliant with AML/CFT standards **cannot acquire significant influence in a PSO**.
Aggregate voting rights and shareholding for such investors are **strictly capped below 20%**.
**Voluntary Surrender & Cooling-off:**
Mandates formalized exit, consumer escrow settlement, and cooling-off frameworks for entities voluntarily surrendering PSO authorisations.
examFocus: License validity: Perpetual for new compliant PSOs (1-year conditional for deficient operators).
FATF non-compliant jurisdiction investment cap: Aggregate voting rights strictly below 20%.

indias-external-debt-reaches-7628-billio.atomicRecall: India's External Debt Reaches $762.8 Billion at End-March 2026 (20.8% of GDP) → $762.8 billion

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) released India's external debt data for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, showing total external debt increased by **$26.3 billion** over end-March 2025 to reach **$762.8 billion**, raising the external debt-to-GDP ratio to **20.8%** (up from 19.8% in 2025).
mustMemorizeFacts: Total External Debt: **$762.8 billion** (Debt-to-GDP: **20.8%**).
Maturity Profile:
Long-Term Debt (>1 year): **$613.5 billion** (80.4% of total debt, up $11.6B).
Short-Term Debt (≤1 year): **$149.3 billion** (Share rose to **19.6%** from 18.3%).
Short-Term Debt to Forex Reserves: Rose to **21.6%** (from 20.1% in 2025).
Debt Service Ratio: Declined to **5.8%** of current receipts (improved from 6.6% in 2025).
Currency Composition:
US Dollar: **55.5%** (Largest currency component).
Indian Rupee: **29.4%** (Second largest).
Institutional Borrower Share:
Non-Financial Corporations: **36.4%** (Largest debtor group).
Deposit-Taking Corporations (excl. RBI): **26.5%**.
General Government: **22.0%**.
Other Financial Corporations: **10.2%**.
Instrument Breakdown: Loans (**34.7%**), Currency & Deposits (**22.3%**), Trade Credit & Advances (**19.0%**), Debt Securities (**16.1%**).
knowUnderstandContext: Valuation Impact vs Real Borrowing: Valuation gains from US dollar appreciation against the Indian rupee and other major currencies amounted to **$24.6 billion**; excluding this valuation effect, the actual increase in external debt would have been **$51.0 billion**.

Private Sector Leverage Shift: General government external debt declined during the year, meaning the entire increase in external debt was driven by corporate, commercial bank, and private non-banking financial institution borrowings.
examFocus: Debt-to-GDP Ratio: 20.8% (end-March 2026).
Debt Service Ratio: 5.8% of current receipts.

rbi-final-directions-on-trade-receivable.atomicRecall: RBI Final Directions on Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) 2026 & ₹25 Cr Net Worth Mandate

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: On the occasion of International MSME Day 2026, the RBI issued the master **"Reserve Bank of India (Trade Receivables Discounting System) Directions, 2026"**, enacting the most comprehensive regulatory overhaul of TReDS since its inception in 2014 under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
1. **Seller Due Diligence Abolished**: Removed mandatory due diligence for MSME sellers to speed up onboarding.
2. **Participant Expansion**: Allowed insurance companies and government-notified credit guarantee funds (e.g., NCGTC) to participate.
3. **Credit Guarantee Protection**: Financiers permitted to obtain credit guarantee cover for factoring units without passing insurance costs to MSME sellers.
4. **Operator Net Worth Standard**: Minimum net worth for TReDS platform operators fixed at **₹25 crore** (existing operators given compliance window till **March 31, 2028**).
5. **Without-Recourse Protection**: All TReDS transactions continue strictly without recourse to MSME sellers.
mustMemorizeFacts: 5 Core Regulatory Shifts:
Mandatory Onboarding Threshold: All companies with turnover **>₹250 crore** and all Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are mandatorily required to register on TReDS.
Active TReDS Platforms (5 Platforms): RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart, C2treds, and DTX (KredX).
knowUnderstandContext: Frictionless MSME Access: Eliminates the mandatory seller due diligence requirement for MSME suppliers, while expanding eligible platform participants to include insurance companies and government credit guarantee funds.
examFocus: TReDS Operator Minimum Net Worth: ₹25 crore (Compliance deadline: March 31, 2028).
Mandatory Onboarding Turnover: >₹250 crore.
Recourse Rule: Without recourse to MSME sellers.
Total Active Platforms: 5 authorized platforms.

Direct Board Interaction: The CRO, CCO, and HIA must meet the Board or Audit/Risk Committee **at least once every quarter without the presence of senior management**.
Dual Reporting: Report **functionally to the Board / Board Committees** and **administratively to the MD & CEO**.
knowUnderstandContext: Supervisory Independence Standard: To prevent operational interference by business heads, the heads of Risk, Compliance, and Audit are granted direct, unhindered functional reporting lines to the Board with protected tenure.
examFocus: Mandatory Control Positions: CRO, CCO, HIA.
Hierarchy Cap: Not more than 2 levels below MD & CEO.

#### What Happened
The Government of India promulgated the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026** (effective April 1, 2026), granting full tax exemptions to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) on Government Securities (G-Secs) while expanding the **Fully Accessible Route (FAR)**.

#### Know / Understand
- **Global Index Inflow Catalysts**: Eliminates withholding taxes and capital gains tax frictions on sovereign bonds to attract an estimated $40–50 billion in institutional capital into Indian debt markets.

#### Must Memorize
- **Tax Exemptions (w.e.f. April 1, 2026)**:
  - **Interest Income on G-Secs**: **100% Tax-Exempt** (previously taxed at 20%).
  - **Capital Gains on G-Secs**: **100% Tax-Exempt** on sale, transfer, or redemption (previously 30% STCG and 12.5% LTCG).
- **FAR Scope Expansion**:
  - Expanded to include new issuances of **15-year, 30-year, and 40-year G-Secs** and **Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs)** in FAR-eligible tenors.
- **General Route Streamlining**:
  - Short-term investment limits, concentration limits, and security-wise caps removed.
  - Overall investment ceilings preserved: **6% of outstanding Central G-Secs** and **2% of State Government Securities (SGSs)**.
  - 'General' and 'Long-Term' FPI sub-categories merged into a single limit.

#### Exam Focus
- FPI G-Sec Tax Status: 100% exempt from interest tax and capital gains tax.
- New FAR Tenors Added: 15-year, 30-year, 40-year G-Secs & Sovereign Green Bonds.
- G-Sec Macro Cap: 6% of Central G-Secs, 2% of State G-Secs.

rbi-releases-draft-capital-adequacy-amen.contentMarkdown:
### 1. RBI Releases Draft Capital Adequacy Amendment Directions & Basel Pillar 3 Market Disclosures
- **Category**: `BANKING_REGULATION`
- **Institution**: `RESERVE_BANK_OF_INDIA`
- **Priority**: `P1_CRITICAL_DEEP`
- **Date**: `2026-05-15`
- **Target Exams**: `SBI PO Mains, IBPS PO Mains`
- **Revision Effort**: `~8 min`
- **Source**: `Smartkeeda (May 2026 Monthly)`

#### What Happened
The Reserve Bank of India unveiled the draft "Reserve Bank of India (Capital Adequacy) Amendment Directions, 2026" and standardized reporting templates to align domestic banking disclosures with the revised **Basel Pillar 3 Market Discipline framework** issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS).

#### Know / Understand
- **Objective of Pillar 3 Upgrades**: To enhance transparency, prevent regulatory arbitrage, and provide standardized, comparable data to depositors, market participants, and rating agencies regarding bank capital buffers, credit risk models, counterparty credit risk, and liquidity ratios.
- **Key Regulatory Thresholds**:
  - **Minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)**: Maintained at **9.0%** for commercial banks (11.5% including Capital Conservation Buffer).
  - **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET-1) Ratio**: Minimum **5.5%**.
  - **Tier-1 Capital Ratio**: Minimum **7.0%**.
  - **Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB)**: **2.50%** comprised entirely of CET-1.
  - **Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB)**: Maintained at **0%** for May 2026.

#### Must Memorize

rbi-increases-borrowing-limits-against-s.contentMarkdown:
### 1. RBI Increases Borrowing Limits Against Securities: ₹1 Crore for Shares & ₹25 Lakh for IPOs
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-04-03
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* The Reserve Bank of India revised the regulatory framework for individual borrowing against securities, substantially enhancing borrowing ceilings to facilitate orderly capital market participation while instituting system-wide risk limits.
* **Implementation Deadline:** The implementation date for the revised capital market exposure framework has been deferred to **July 1, 2026**.

#### Must Memorize
* **Enhanced Individual Borrowing Ceilings:**
  * **Loans Against Shares & Eligible Securities (REITs/InvITs):** Raised from ₹20 lakh to **₹1 crore per borrower**.
  * **IPO, FPO, and ESOP Subscriptions:** Raised from ₹10 lakh to **₹25 lakh per individual**.
* **System-Wide Aggregate Cap:**
  * Borrowing limits now apply as an **aggregate system-wide cap across the entire banking sector**, rather than per individual lending institution, preventing borrowers from bypassing exposure limits by obtaining multiple loans across different banks.
* **Removal of Regulatory Ceiling on Listed Debt:**
  * The regulatory ceiling on bank lending against **listed debt securities** has been completely removed.
* **Standard Margin Requirements:**
  * **Physical Shares:** Minimum margin of **50%**.
  * **Dematerialised (Demat) Shares:** Minimum margin of **25%**.

#### Know / Understand
* Previously, investors could take ₹20 lakh from multiple banks simultaneously to finance speculative share purchases. By converting the cap into a PAN-linked system-wide limit of ₹1 crore (and ₹25 lakh for IPOs), RBI balances retail liquidity access with macroprudential safety.

#### Exam Focus
* Loans against shares ceiling: ₹1 crore per borrower (earlier ₹20 lakh).
* IPO/FPO/ESOP financing limit: ₹25 lakh per individual (earlier ₹10 lakh).
* System-wide cap rule preventing multi-bank borrowing.
* Margin requirements: 50% for physical shares and 25% for demat shares.
* Implementation effective date: July 1, 2026.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**
Government of India launched Phase I of **Census 2027** on April 1, 2026, ending a 16-year gap (the longest in independent India's history since 2011).
**Historical Milestones:**
**16th Census overall** and **8th since Independence**.
**First fully digital census** conducted via mobile apps and online portals.
**First caste enumeration across all communities since 1931** (colonial-era censuses included caste from 1881 to 1931).
**Two-Phase Architecture & Budget:**
**Total Budget Outlay:** **₹11,718.24 crore**.
**Phase I (April–September 2026):** House Listing and Housing Census (condition of houses, amenities, assets).
**Phase II (February 2027):** Population Enumeration (demographics, socio-economic status, education, migration, fertility, caste).

**Operational Metrics:** 33-question survey; self-enumeration portal in 16 languages; generates an 11-digit unique Self-Enumeration (SE) ID; covers 36 States/UTs, 7,092 sub-districts, and ~6.4 lakh villages under a 'Census-as-a-Service' model.
**Exam Focus:** ₹11,718.24 Cr outlay, 16th census / 8th post-independence, 1st digital & 1st caste enumeration since 1931, 2 phases (House Listing Apr-Sep 2026, Population Feb 2027).

rbi-mandates-two-factor-authentication-2.atomicRecall: RBI Mandates Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for All Digital Payments

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**

Reserve Bank of India rolled out comprehensive directions making **Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) mandatory** for all domestic online transactions, including UPI, debit/credit cards, and prepaid mobile wallets.

**Authentication Requirements:** A one-time password (OTP) alone is no longer sufficient; transactions require at least two distinct authentication factors (e.g., PIN/password + biometric fingerprint/facial recognition or OTP).
**Customer Protection & Systemic Liability:** Financial institutions are held liable to compensate customers for unauthorized transactions caused by system or security infrastructure failures.
**Cross-Border Scope:** Phased implementation roadmap extends authentication norms to international cross-border card transactions by **October 2026**.
**Exam Focus:** Mandatory 2FA for all digital payment channels; multi-factor verification beyond standalone OTP; October 2026 international transaction deadline.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**
India officially resumed importing crude oil and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) from Iran after a **7-year hiatus** dating back to May 2019 following US sanctions.

**Initial Shipments:** LPG carrier *Sea Bird* (44,000 MT) docked at Mangaluru Port; supertankers *MT Jaya* and *MT Felicity* discharged 4 million barrels of crude at Paradip and Sikka ports under a 30-day US sanctions waiver.

**Payment Settlement Mechanism:** Transactions are settled entirely in **Indian Rupees (INR) using Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA)** maintained at **UCO Bank** and non-sanctioned Iranian banking institutions, bypassing the US dollar clearing system.
**Strategic Maritime Context:** Around 40–50% of India's crude imports pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
**Exam Focus:** Resumption after 7 years (since May 2019), Rupee settlement via UCO Bank Vostro accounts, Mangaluru/Paradip/Sikka delivery ports.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**

Reserve Bank of India issued a comprehensive consolidated Master Direction on Notes and Coins Exchange Facility under Section 45 of the RBI Act, 1934 and Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, advancing the **Clean Note Policy**.
**Expanded Soiled Note Definition:** Includes two-piece notes that are fully intact when pasted together; banks must accept them at counters for credit/exchange but cannot reissue them to the public.
**Performance-Linked Incentive & Subsidy Scheme:**
**Capital Expenditure Reimbursement:** Up to **100% of capex (capped at ₹50 lakh per Currency Chest)** for CCs set up in North-Eastern regions, J&K, and Ladakh.
**Revenue Subsidy:** **50% operational cost reimbursement** for the first 5 years.
**Exchange Incentives:** ₹2 per packet for soiled notes of ₹50 and below; ₹2 per piece for mutilated note adjudication; ₹65/bag (urban) and ₹75/bag (rural/semi-urban) for coin distribution.
**Dispute Escalation:** Unresolved currency exchange grievances escalate after 30 days to the **RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (CMS portal)**.
**Exam Focus:** Two-piece soiled note rules, ₹50 lakh Currency Chest capex subsidy in NE/hilly regions, coin distribution incentives (₹65/₹75 per bag), 30-day ombudsman escalation.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**

Union Cabinet approved the establishment of the **Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMI Pool)** with a financial outlay of **₹12,980 crore** to reduce reliance on foreign marine underwriters and secure Indian merchant shipping.
**Coverage Scope:** Provides comprehensive domestic underwriting for:
**Hull & Machinery Insurance** (physical ship structures).
**Cargo Insurance** (goods in maritime transit).
**Protection & Indemnity (P&I)** (third-party crew and environmental liability).
**War Risk Insurance** (vessels operating in high-risk corridors and conflict zones).

**Strategic Significance:** India handles 95% of international trade by volume and 70% by value via maritime routes; aligns India with state-backed maritime insurance frameworks in the UK, Japan, and South Korea.
**Exam Focus:** BMI Pool outlay (₹12,980 Cr), 4 insurance lines (Hull, Cargo, P&I, War Risk), 95% trade volume dependency.

**Blue Bin:** Dry Waste (Recyclables).
**Red Bin:** Sanitary Waste.
**Black Bin:** Special Care / Domestic Hazardous Waste.

national-administrative-initiatives-rost.title: National & Administrative Initiatives Roster (April 2026)

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Implementing nodal ministry or statutory agency
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

mustMemorizeFacts: **MoPNG National PNG Drive 2.0:** Extended till June 30, 2026 by PNGRB to increase natural gas share in India's energy basket to 15% by 2030 (>3.1 lakh connections gasified in March 2026).

**DoT SIM-Binding Deadline Extension:** Extended OTT platform SIM-binding deadline to December 31, 2026 (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal); revoked mandatory 6-hour web session auto-logout in favor of risk-based fraud triggers.
**MoSPI SDG Dashboard & e-Sankhyiki Portal:** Developed in partnership with UN Resident Coordinator Office (UNRCO) for tracking National Indicator Framework time-series data.

**Nagoya Protocol Compliance Leadership:** India issued 3,561 Internationally Recognized Certificates of Compliance (IRCCs) under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (accounting for 56% of all 6,311 IRCCs globally; France #2 with 964).

**Tea Board "Tea Mark" Quality Certification:** Rolled out voluntary supply-chain traceability certification under Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 (India is 2nd largest global tea producer / 1st in black tea).
**NMDC Iron Ore Landmark:** Produced 53.15 MT iron ore in FY26 (+21%), becoming the first mining company in India's history to cross the 50 MT annual milestone (Kirandul, Bacheli, Donimalai mines).

**MHA Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) Reclassification:** Total LWE-affected districts remained at 38 under the SRE Scheme, with active red corridor contracting to 2 districts ('LWE Affected') and 35 'Legacy & Thrust' districts (₹1,685.65 Cr released over 5 years).
**Indian Railways Asset Monetisation:** Earned record ₹6,735 crore from scrap disposal in FY26 (+12% above ₹6,000 Cr target) across 5,053 e-auctions (South Central Railway top at ₹641.92 Cr).

**Customs Duty Exemption on 40 Petrochemicals:** Full basic customs duty waiver till June 30, 2026 on 40 critical feedstocks (methanol, toluene, styrene, MEG) with ₹1,800 crore forgone revenue to cushion West Asia supply shocks.

**NCERT Granted Deemed University Status:** Ministry of Education and UGC granted deemed-to-be-university status under the 'De Novo' category to NCERT and its 6 constituent regional units (RIEs at Ajmer, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Mysuru, Shillong + PSSCIVE Bhopal), enabling degree-granting powers and Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) integration.

**Namo Drone Didi SHG Pilot Standings:** Karnataka leads India with 145 trained women SHG drone pilots under the ₹1,261 crore central sector scheme (Prayagraj top district with 16 pilots; 15,000 agricultural drones target).
**India Annual Wind Capacity Addition Record:** Installed record 6.05 GW wind capacity in FY26 (+46% YoY), taking cumulative installed wind power capacity past 56 GW (India ranks 4th globally).
**Amul Reaches ₹1 Trillion Turnover:** Amul/GCMMF became India's 1st FMCG enterprise to cross ₹1 lakh crore turnover in FY26 (reported revenue ₹73,450 Cr, +11.4% YoY).

**ICAR Task Force on Agricultural Resilience:** Established high-level Special Task Force under DARE/ICAR to scale 'Mera Gaon Mera Gaurav' across 100 aspirational districts and promote Direct Seeding of Rice (DSR).
**Skills Outcomes Fund (₹530 Cr):** Launched by MSDE and NSDC under outcomes-based financing (OBF) to provide employment-linked training for 2 lakh youth across BFSI, IT-ITeS, and Green Jobs.

**Minimum Export Price on Natural Honey:** Extended floor price of $1,400 per metric ton until December 31, 2026 (ITC HS 04090000) under National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (UP leads production with 17%).
**GeM Womaniya Initiative FY26 Volume:** Secured 13.7 lakh public procurement orders worth thousands of crores across >2 lakh registered women-led Micro & Small Enterprises.

**Rajya Sabha Panel of Vice-Chairpersons Reconstituted:** 6 members nominated by Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan: Dinesh Sharma, S. Phangnon Konyak, Ghanshyam Tiwari (BJP); Phulo Devi Netam (INC); M. Thambidurai (AIADMK); Sasmit Patra (BJD).

**MeitY AI Governance Group (AIGEG) & TPEC:** Constituted inter-ministerial AI Governance and Economic Group chaired by Ashwini Vaishnaw and supported by the Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) chaired by MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan.

**Tata Semiconductor Dholera SEZ Notified:** Ministry of Commerce notified 66.17-hectare SEZ for Tata Electronics-PSMC Taiwan ₹91,000 crore semiconductor fabrication plant (50,000 wafers/month, commercial chips by Dec 2026).

**Central Government DA/DR 2% Hike:** Approved 2% Dearness Allowance/Dearness Relief hike effective January 1, 2026 (raising DA to 60% of basic pay, costing ₹6,791.24 Cr annually for 50.46L employees and 68.27L pensioners under 7th CPC).
**MoEFCC-NBA Grassroots Biodiversity Project:** 5-year $4.88 million project with GEF and UNDP across Sathyamangalam (TN) and Nokrek/Garo Hills (Meghalaya) landscapes.
**Vibrant Village Programme-II in J&K:** 6 border villages in Kathua district (Bobiya, Kadyala, Gajnal, Karol Krishna, Rathua, Gujjar Chak) covered under VVP-II (₹6,839 Cr outlay up to FY29).

**Supreme Court 'Right to Safe Road Travel' Ruling:** Bench ruled Right to Safe Road Travel is an integral part of Article 21 ('In Re: Phalodi Accident'), prohibiting commercial structures within NH rights-of-way and ordering 60-day removal.

**Uttar Pradesh 'Jal Arpan' 10-Year O&M Warranty:** UP became 1st state to mandate 10-year contractor operation and maintenance warranty for rural piped water supply under Jal Jeevan Mission, shifting ownership to Gram Panchayats.
**SkyHop Aviation Seaplane AOC:** DGCA granted commercial Air Operator Certificate to SkyHop Aviation using DHC-6 Twin Otter aircraft to connect 5 Lakshadweep islands.
**Ladakh District Expansion:** Approved creation of 5 new districts (Nubra, Sham, Changthang, Zanskar, Drass), expanding Ladakh from 2 to 7 administrative districts.
**Punjab 'Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna':** Approved ₹1,000/month financial assistance for women (₹1,500/month for SC women) with ₹9,300 crore budget allocation for FY 2026-27.
**Andhra Pradesh Weaver Power Subsidy Scheme:** ₹150 crore scheme providing up to 200 units/month free electricity for handlooms and 500 units/month for powerlooms, plus ₹4,000 weaver pension.
**AICTE-VAANI 3rd Edition:** ₹4 crore annual scheme supporting 200 conferences in 22 regional languages across 16 emerging tech thrust domains.
**CAPF General Administration Act 2026:** Notified statutory quota reserving 50% IG, 67% ADG, and 100% SDG/DG posts across 7 CAPFs for Indian Police Service (IPS) officers on deputation.
**Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance 2026:** Conferred official language status on Khasi and Garo languages alongside English, repealing the 2005 Act.
**India Withdraws COP 33 (2028) Hosting Bid:** Formally withdrew its bid to host the 2028 UN Climate Summit, leaving South Korea as the sole Asia-Pacific bidder.

* **NCERT Granted Deemed University Status:** Ministry of Education and UGC granted deemed-to-be-university status under the 'De Novo' category to NCERT and its 6 constituent regional units (RIEs at Ajmer, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Mysuru, Shillong + PSSCIVE Bhopal), enabling degree-granting powers and Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) integration.

* **ICAR Task Force on Agricultural Resilience:** Established high-level Special Task Force under DARE/ICAR to scale 'Mera Gaon Mera Gaurav' across 100 aspirational districts and promote Direct Seeding of Rice (DSR).

* **GeM Womaniya Initiative FY26 Volume:** Secured 13.7 lakh public procurement orders worth thousands of crores across >2 lakh registered women-led Micro & Small Enterprises.
* **Rajya Sabha Panel of Vice-Chairpersons Reconstituted:** 6 members nominated by Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan: Dinesh Sharma, S. Phangnon Konyak, Ghanshyam Tiwari (BJP); Phulo Devi Netam (INC); M. Thambidurai (AIADMK); Sasmit Patra (BJD).

* **Tata Semiconductor Dholera SEZ Notified:** Ministry of Commerce notified 66.17-hectare SEZ for Tata Electronics-PSMC Taiwan ₹91,000 crore semiconductor fabrication plant (50,000 wafers/month, commercial chips by Dec 2026).
* **Central Government DA/DR 2% Hike:** Approved 2% Dearness Allowance/Dearness Relief hike effective January 1, 2026 (raising DA to 60% of basic pay, costing ₹6,791.24 Cr annually for 50.46L employees and 68.27L pensioners under 7th CPC).
* **MoEFCC-NBA Grassroots Biodiversity Project:** 5-year $4.88 million project with GEF and UNDP across Sathyamangalam (TN) and Nokrek/Garo Hills (Meghalaya) landscapes.
* **Vibrant Village Programme-II in J&K:** 6 border villages in Kathua district (Bobiya, Kadyala, Gajnal, Karol Krishna, Rathua, Gujjar Chak) covered under VVP-II (₹6,839 Cr outlay up to FY29).

* **Ladakh District Expansion:** Approved creation of 5 new districts (Nubra, Sham, Changthang, Zanskar, Drass), expanding Ladakh from 2 to 7 administrative districts.
* **Punjab 'Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna':** Approved ₹1,000/month financial assistance for women (₹1,500/month for SC women) with ₹9,300 crore budget allocation for FY 2026-27.
* **Andhra Pradesh Weaver Power Subsidy Scheme:** ₹150 crore scheme providing up to 200 units/month free electricity for handlooms and 500 units/month for powerlooms, plus ₹4,000 weaver pension.
* **AICTE-VAANI 3rd Edition:** ₹4 crore annual scheme supporting 200 conferences in 22 regional languages across 16 emerging tech thrust domains.
